journeys.consumer: graph, tensor-kernel or inference execution layer
journeys.topology: one already-admitted root runs 16 finite batches; each batch exposes 128 indexed, non-suspending work items to four provider workers, each item computes one deterministic 1024-element tile, and the root returns only after the whole batch is quiescent
journeys.ownership: the root owns immutable input and 128 stable result slots; workers borrow the callable, input and slots only until batch completion; the provider owns execution metadata but no individual result, future or detached lifetime

normal_shape.cancellation: one dormant batch-level source or provider cancellation domain

charged_phases: 1024-element deterministic tile compute for every indexed item
write to caller-owned stable result slot
one whole-batch completion and exact result consumption
excluded_setup: root admission and one complete warmup batch

sources.status: Graph is QUEUED; this proves only the range/fan-out consumer shape and grants no Graph verdict.

external_provenance.observation: Both CPU runtimes execute a finite graph/kernel episode with shared completion, abort/control state and chunk allocation rather than one independently owned future per chunk.

journeys.reason: A 1024-element floor comes from the current Graph consumer and matches tile-sized inference work. It prevents a noop or queue-only benchmark from choosing the public API while retaining enough batches to expose dispatch and completion cost.

common.result_granularity: one caller-owned uint64 result slot per indexed work item
common.completion_granularity: one synchronous completion per batch; all work is quiescent before the next batch
common.failure: normal replay has no body failure and no admission failure
common.cancellation: normal replay never requests cancellation; no side pays per-item cancellation ownership
common.suspension: work bodies never suspend or block
common.lifetime: input, callable and result slots remain valid for the complete synchronous batch
common.parallelism: four pinned provider worker threads; the external process role never executes a tile
common.accounting: 2048 exact item callbacks and one identical checksum

hyle.root_wait: the admitted Scheduler Fiber suspends on the batch Event
hyle.metadata: one caller-stack batch state, at most four raw runners and one shared atomic cursor

marl.route: Scheduler::enqueue one Task per indexed item plus one WaitGroup per batch
marl.root_wait: the admitted Marl task/fiber waits on the batch WaitGroup
marl.metadata: Marl owns its natural Task records and group state; caller retains result slots

onetbb.route: task_arena(max_concurrency=4) plus parallel_for blocked_range grain=1 and simple_partitioner
onetbb.root_wait: one enqueued arena root executes the synchronous parallel_for; provider task-helping is an implementation mechanism inside the same four-worker ceiling
onetbb.metadata: oneTBB owns partition/task metadata; caller retains result slots

negative_space.noop_or_queue_only: Zero-work and queue-only rows are mechanism diagnostics and cannot gate this product route.
negative_space.rich_per_task: schedule_task/JoinHandle retains independent typed result/status/cancel ownership and is not a peer for this journey.
negative_space.adaptive_algorithms: Partitioners, reduce/scan/sort, graph policy and tensor kernels remain Graph/algorithm responsibilities.
negative_space.downstream_closure: Building IO, Compute or Graph against sched proves compatibility only; it does not validate their functionality or performance.
